angle: Proof-first surprise, told as a test scenario: dinner for 2 vegetarians with no oven, and the vague prompt got oven-roasted chicken in both runs. The AI is a stranger in your kitchen, so write the prompt like a recipe card. The card is built line by line, with a real output snippet as proof on each step.

slides.body: I never told it who was eating. The AI wasn't the problem. My prompt was.

slides.headline: AI is a stranger in your kitchen
slides.body: It didn't grow up there, so it guessed. Run 2 even said: "If you tell me … what's in your fridge, I can tailor it."

slides.headline: Same AI. Recipe-card prompt. The right dinner.
slides.body: "Palak paneer moong dal (serves 2, about 25 minutes)". No oven. Every ingredient in grams. "about 34 g per serving" (AI's estimate).

slides.headline: 1-2. Who's eating, what's in the kitchen
slides.body: Serves = who it is for. Ingredients = what you already have. It came back with: "Paneer: 200 g, in 1.5 cm cubes".
slides.visual: Frame 0 shows the headline and a blank recipe card. Over 6 seconds, two lines write themselves onto the card: "Serves: 2 people, vegetarian, about 30 g protein each." and "Ingredients … 200 g paneer, moong dal … No oven.", with a tiny label "test prompt, trimmed". slides.headline: 3-4. The shape, and an example
slides.body: Method = the answer's shape. Tastes like = one example to aim at. It came back with: "Sear the paneer (3 minutes, during step 1)."
slides.visual: The same recipe card now also shows lines 3 and 4: "Method … numbered steps with grams for every ingredient and minutes for every step …" and "Tastes like: dal tadka, but lighter.", with a tiny label "test prompt, trimmed". slides.headline: 5-6. Limits. Then taste before serving.
slides.body: Don't = your limits. Taste and adjust = it checks its maths, then asks: "Will you eat this on its own, or with rice or roti?"

Over 8 seconds, a note pinned to a fridge door draws on beside Don't with three crossed-out kitchen items: a deep-frying kadhai, a cream carton and a kitchen timer past 30. A tasting spoon then draws on beside Taste and adjust, with a typewriter snippet "…so it clears the 30 g goal." tagged "AI's estimate", and a speech bubble from the robot chef with the roti question. Both carry a tiny label "real run 1, trimmed". A handwritten margin line draws on last, underlined in yellow: "Maa tastes before serving. So should AI."

slides.headline: Save this: the recipe-card prompt
slides.body: Serves: who it's for. Ingredients: what you have. Method: answer shape. Tastes like: an example. Don't: limits. Taste and adjust: self-check, one question.

caption:
Dinner for 2 vegetarians. No oven. The AI's answer: lemon-garlic chicken, roasted at 220°C.

That was my test scenario, and I never told the AI any of it. I only typed "Give me a healthy dinner recipe". I ran it twice and got chicken and an oven both times. It even added a vegetarian swap and a no-oven swap, because it had to guess.

The AI wasn't wrong. It is a stranger in your kitchen. My prompt was a family recipe: a pinch of this, cook till done. That only works if you grew up there.

So I wrote the prompt like a proper recipe card. Six lines:
Serves: who it is for
Ingredients: what you already have
Method: the shape of the answer you want
Tastes like: one example to aim at
Don't: your limits
Taste and adjust: it checks its own work and asks you one question

Same model, same day, each prompt run twice. The recipe card got a paneer, palak and moong dal dish both times: no oven, 25 to 27 minutes, ingredients in grams, a time on every step, and one question back at the end. Maa tastes before serving. So should AI.

Two honest notes. The "about 34 g per serving" protein figure is the AI's own estimate, not verified nutrition. And this was a prompt test, not a cooked meal.
